formats.key: Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: Once anyone submits the signature, the USDS allowance from the owner (the signer) to `spender` is set to exactly `value`. It replaces any earlier allowance and does not add to it (Usds.sol permit: `allowance[owner][spender] = value`).
The signature works only until `deadline` (`require(block.timestamp <= deadline)`). It is single-use, because `nonces[owner]++` consumes the nonce.
If `value` is type(uint256).max, the allowance is never reduced when the spender uses it (transferFrom and burn skip the decrement). That makes it an unlimited right to move or burn the owner's USDS.
With this allowance the spender can move USDS out of the owner's balance with transferFrom, or burn it with burn(from, value).
formats.shown: The intent "Authorize spending of tokens", then the spender address in raw hex, the max amount in USDS ("Unlimited" at or above 2^255), the expiry date and the owner address.

findings.title: Permit has no interpolatedIntent, so the intent names no token, amount or spender.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json display.formats Permit: "intent": "Authorize spending of tokens" with no interpolatedIntent; FORMATS.md: interpolatedIntent: null. Case 0 screen intent: "Authorize spending of tokens".
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent such as "Allow {spender} to spend up to {value} until {deadline}".
